MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "Lateralus feels like my most natural next choice after 10.000 Days because I want more of Tool's immersive sound and intricate rhythms.",
    "Hybrid Theory and Vol. 3 fit my interest in heavy guitars balanced with memorable melodies; aggression alone is not what makes them appealing.",
    "Believe connects with my recent interest in Ten Thousand Fists, while City of Evil appeals to the elaborate guitar playing I enjoy in Advance And Vanquish."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "St. Anger offers heaviness, but its raw, repetitive approach misses the melodic detail or rhythmic complexity I want right now.",
    "Chocolate Starfish emphasizes rap-rock swagger more than the melodic metal and intricate playing I am currently seeking.",
    "The Marshall Mathers feels disconnected from my current interest in guitar-driven music; intensity by itself does not make it a natural next listen."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "The recommendations seem to treat loudness and aggression as enough to connect albums, although the balance of melody, rhythm and guitar work matters more to me.",
    "My interest in some accessible heavy rock seems to have been stretched into a broader interest in rap-centered music than my recent choices support."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "My latest choice of 10.000 Days makes immersive, rhythmically intricate music especially appealing today, which is why Lateralus stands out above the rest.",
    "I can enjoy both accessible hooks and extreme heaviness, but I prefer each to offer musical detail rather than relying mainly on attitude.",
    "An album can fit my taste without being something I choose immediately: Meteora and Believe appeal to me, but today I would prioritize Lateralus, Hybrid Theory and Vol. 3."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The recommendations understood my interest in heavy music but sometimes overlooked the melody, intricate playing and recent pull toward Tool that determine what I want next."
}
